evidence_quality.consequence: Every competitor fact is 'per search summary'. No same-day competitor USD sell rate was obtained, so effective markup could be computed only for ChatGPT Plus (4 official-like points) and, as explicit fee percentages, for three card/FX structures. All other distributions are null or priors.
evidence_quality.rerun_requirements: Raise the session web-search cap (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION) and allow the competitor hosts under the environment Network access (Allowed domains); then run the queries in docs/03-research/07-ir-competitors.md Appendix B and the mystery-shopper protocol in section 8.

how_to_consume: A null Record means unknown: do not substitute a default silently. Use the sibling *_sim_prior Record (clearly flagged UNVERIFIED) only inside the simulator and always run the sensitivity sweep over its low/high.
price_observations with include_in_stats=false are kept for audit but excluded from markup_stats.
markup_stats, elasticity.derived_grid, market_size.low/base/high and market_size.derived are produced by scripts/research/07_markup_stats.py --write; re-run it after adding observations.

method.form: mixed multinomial logit over a consideration set: U_ij = -b_p[s] * ln(P_ij / P_ref) + b_t[s] * trust_j + b_v[s] * speed_j + e_ij
calibration_identities: Lerner inversion for a profit-maximising seller: |e_firm| = 1 / m, m = (P - MC) / P
Share after an undercut d (fraction) from share s: s' = s*x / (1 - s + s*x), x = exp(|e_firm| / (1 - s) * d)
method.uncertainty: No empirical elasticity could be estimated in this run (no volume data, 0 pages read directly). Priors below bracket the logic and must be calibrated with first-party A/B tests and competitor mystery-shopping.

price.verify_how: Run +/-2% and +/-5% price-point experiments on our own quote page (randomised by session) and regress conversion on log price ratio vs the lowest visible competitor; at least 2,000 quote views per arm.

price_sim_prior.verify_how: Calibrate on first-party experiments; until then treat as a sensitivity axis, not a fact.
price_sim_prior.note: modelling assumption, NOT an observation. Built from segment priors below (share-weighted: 0.30*-20 + 0.40*-8 + 0.30*-2 = -9.8). Lerner inversion with observed explicit margins of 2-6% would imply |e| of 17-50 for pure price-takers, so the prior is deliberately lower (information frictions, trust).

price_war.note: No dated undercutting episode was found in the collected evidence. The items below are mechanisms and hypotheses to be tested, not history.

patterns.statement: Sellers with a live rate feed re-price within one tick of a rival move.
patterns.evidence: Dollarisho claims a live Bonbast rate; Cafearz advertises live prices [S13, S41].
patterns.sim_hint: Model API-driven sellers as matching within <=1 rates tick (5 min) down to their floor.
patterns.verify_how: Record a rival's price every 30 min for 24 h during a volatile session.

patterns.statement: Catalog-priced shops (gift cards, subscriptions) re-price in hours to days.
patterns.evidence: Emalls shows listings last updated 6 hours to 2 days ago [S35].
patterns.sim_hint: Model catalog sellers re-pricing every 6-48 h; undercut window lasts until the next catalog edit.

patterns.statement: Incumbents answer with trust, speed or guarantees rather than price.
patterns.evidence: Titles stress 'instant', 'guarantee', 'lowest fee', 'since X years' [S37]; incumbents invest in sponsored media [S27, S28].
patterns.sim_hint: Model trust-led segment as inelastic; incumbents hold share until their cost floor is hit.
patterns.verify_how: Interview customers who switched; compare share before/after.

patterns.statement: Under visible-price pressure sellers shift value between rate, percentage fee and fixed fee.
patterns.evidence: Three different structures coexist (A, B, C) [S10, S13, S14].
patterns.sim_hint: Let competitor agents draw a structure archetype; undercutting on the headline lever while raising a minor one.
patterns.verify_how: Compare all-in cost for the same basket across structures at USD 50/100/500/1000.

patterns.statement: Percentage-fee sellers have little room: explicit fees (4-6%) are already close to a reseller's cost floor (~7% over market for a USD 100 load in our own model).
patterns.evidence: Computed in 07_markup_stats.py from the lead's cost model [S09] and observed fees.
patterns.sim_hint: A sustained undercut larger than (observed fee - cost floor) forces a rival to lose money; model exit/stop-selling at the floor.
patterns.verify_how: Rebuild the floor with real provider fees once measured (brief 01/12).
